utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Will the registrar please have the accused brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I greet, once again, the interpreters who were greeted this morning, they are the same, I understand. Let us now resume. First of all, I would like to present my apologies because we are beginning late. Sometimes I'm not trying to give you explanations, but you should understand there is some formal procedures we must follow, but please understand that sometimes I am required to attend to other matters dealing, in particular, with the Trial Chamber itself. We will proceed until 6.30, if the interpreters are in agreement. We will try to take a break of 15 minutes and then another of 20 minutes. I hope the interpreters agree with that new schedule. I have not received a response from them, I am a bit concerned. The French booth says all right, and the English booth, I see that they are nodding in agreement. Very well, thank you very much. Let us now bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: INTERPRETER: Microphone to the President. Microphone to the President, please The interpreters request that the microphone be turned on in front of the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Nobilo, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we are now going to move to 19 April, and we will try to understand what reports and what orders came to the command on the 19th of April, and I would like the next document to please be distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: First, I would like to ask a question with regards -- of the last statements made by the witness with regards to the 17th of April. You said that the front line of the HVO was at 15 kilometres from the last house in Ahmici. You said 50 metres, rather, 50 meters from Ahmici, near Baringaj, and that the BiH was 150 metres from Ahmici. Was Ahmici at that time in the hands of the HVO or in the hands of the BiH?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the information which His Honour has just stated here are not the exact information which I had given, and with your permission I would like to correct this information. What I had stated is that the HVO line behind the village of Ahmici was about 50 metres. That means approximately 50 metres. And then from that line, the BH army units were at a distance of about 150 metres, rather than about 50 metres, as I believe the interpretation was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I said 150, 150. Now, my follow-up to that question: Ahmici was in the hands of the HVO or the BiH? Speaking now of the city of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On 17 April 1993, there were no BH army units in the village of Ahmici. The units that were there had pushed back the HVO units to the lines which I had stated previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The interpretation is not quite clear. The HVO units were, had pushed the BH army units to a distance of about 200 metres away from Ahmici; is that what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Brigadier, in order to make things perfectly clear, let's move directly to the scale model so that you can explain to the Trial Chamber how you actually used these, how you placed these green flags on this scale model. Brigadier, please show what you were told in the Operative Zone command? What information was arriving on the 17th and 18th of April? Where were the BH army lines? Could you explain to the Trial Chamber, what does this scale model reflect at this time, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, on 17 April 1993, on the basis of combat reports which we received from the field, the BH army units in the territory of the Busovaca and Vitez municipalities were deployed, as is shown by these red flags.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean green flags?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I apologise, the green flags. I have placed them on the basis of the combat reports in order to better reflect the situation which was in Vitez and Busovaca municipalities at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you show the town of Vitez and point to the road, take it along the road all the way to Busovaca so we see the main road?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the town of Vitez is located here on the model. So, the blue flag is the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and the green ones are the command in the old Vitez. And the green flags mark the positions of the BH army, starting from the village of Sadovace, and the village of Grbavica, and then they crossed the road into the village of Grbavica, this is the Vitez Travnik road, in front of the village of Jardo, in front of the village of Krcevine, in front of the Krizancevo Selo, in front of Buhine Kuce, in front of the village of upper Santici, in the village of Pirici, in front of the village of Ahmici, in front of the village of Krtine, on the slopes of Mount Kuber, in front of the village of Loncari, on the feature Gradina, which is part of Mount Kuber, and behind the village of Putis. That means the village of Putis was under the control of the army, and then crossing the Kaonik road, and then the village of Katici, and then around the feature called Kula -- apologies, when I stopped off at Krtine, this is where the Busovaca municipality starts. So, that means it was in front of the feature of Kula, towards the village across this mountain here, towards the village of Solakovici, in front of the village of Nezirovici, that means the Nezirovici village was under control of the BH army, and then between Kacuni and Busovaca, and then in front of Proseje. Proseje was under the HVO control. Across this mountain, this is the Mount Zicka, if I recall correctly; further, in front of the village of Kupres, the village of Kupres was under the HVO control across Mount Kruscica all the way here. In front of the village of, that is, in fact, between the villages of upper and lower Rovna, then the village of Vranjska, part of the village of Kruscica. A large part of the village of Kruscica was under the BH army control and a smaller part was under the control of the HVO. In front of the village of Baskaradi, Baskaradi was under the HVO control, and the area behind it was under the BH army control, towards the Mount Zvjezda all the way to Zabridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, the area which we had not marked, is that part of the Novi Travnik and Travnik municipalities where there were no conflicts on those days in April which we're referring to now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, all this area which I am now pointing out is the area of the municipalities of Novi Travnik and Travnik. There were no fighting with the BH army there in those days, and there were positions only held against the army of the Republika Srpska from the Mount Vlasic to Mount of Mravinjaci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, you have failed to show me the road, Vitez Busovaca. And when you do so, can you please show me the shortest distances between the main road and the frontlines of the BH army, and where were they, the exact locations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Vitez Busovaca road extends along this valley -- just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And this flag, what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I said that these are the BH army forces in the old Vitez area, in Mahala. So, the road extends along this valley, and the narrowest section of it that, is the narrowest spot in relation to the BH army positions from the left and right side of the road, going from Vitez to Busovaca, that means it would be about 1.5 kilometres as the crow flies. This was an area near the village of Ahmici, and on the other side the BiH army positions near the village of Vranjske.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, to the north of the road, the BH army units, and the BH army units which were south of the road; how close, that is, what was the shortest distance to the road of the BH army units in general?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The shortest distance between the road to Vitez Kaonik and the BH army units were at Sivrino Selo. The distance here was no more than 250 metres. This is the position which the BH army units, throughout 1993 until the Washington agreements, in fact, continued to attack and threaten the BH army units which were defending this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. I would now like to ask the technical service to take a picture of this scale model and I would like to tender it into evidence, and I would like it marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just add something. From this picture that is going to be taken of this scale model, you will see that the HVO units in Busovaca and Vitez were practically completely surrounded.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph which will be taken of the scale model will have the number D320, and the document which will be distributed will have the numbers 319, 319A for the French version, and 319B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I'm referring to the D319, and it is a report from the Frankopan Brigade in Travnik. It is a short one, it is directed to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone in Vitez. I'm only going to read the second paragraph, which is relevant here. "In Brajkovici and Grahovcici there are some displaced Croats from Zenica," and then in parentheses it says "1500", "and parts of the units of the Jure Francetic Brigade from Zenica, all of which upsets my plans. The preparations for defence are nearly finalised, all levels have been involved. This is a decisive moment for Croats, and we shall persevere." Commander, I believe the last name is Nakic, I can't read it well, and then it is signed and stamped. Brigadier, first of all, do you recall this report, or a similar report from the Frankopan Brigade? And do you recognise any signatures or stamps here?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do recall the events related in this report. It was compiled in the Frankopan Brigade. It had its command at Guca Gora. It was signed by the commander. I know the commander personally and I recognise his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The 1.500 citizens who found themselves there, could you point to the location where these people were?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This report was drafted after the HVO in Zenica was defeated, after the HVO ceased to exist in the municipal area of Zenica. I can try to show the exact location of Guca Gora. If I don't have it on the map, then I can show it on the scale model.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we please remove the cap from the projector?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you cannot see it, maybe you can just show the wider area.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Unfortunately, there's no Guca Gora marked specifically, but I can show an area, see, this area (indicating), and it's only about 1, 1.5 kilometres from there to Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Can we move on to the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This map has the number 321. The following document is D322, D322A for the French version, and D322B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I am looking at a report of the 111th XP Brigade, and it is addressed, unlike the others, to the attention of Milivoj Petkovic, the Croatian Defence Council in Mostar, and to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in Mostar, and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, to the commander Tihomir Blaskic. I'm reading the top paragraph: "In the zone of responsibility of the 111th XP Brigade, there have been no conflicts with the Muslims and their behaviour is odd. The town of Zepce has been deserted, has been a virtual ghost town for the last two days. Inns owned by Muslim owners are empty. The Islamic troops that have been returned from the checkpoint have left for Z. Polje. I am considering issuing an order on the withdrawal of our forces from the territory of the defence of the town of Maglaj, as a warning for the attacks they are conducting against our forces in Central Bosnia. I have been receiving information on mistreatment of Croats in Zenica about the complete disarmament and search carried out in the village of Crkvica and the confiscation of weapons. We do not have the complete information, nor has the truth about the sufferings of Croats been sufficiently represented in the Croatian media. It is necessary to inform everyone about the suffering of Croats in Zenica," and then I can't read the word, "about the dangers to their property and their personal safety. Establish contact with the church in Zenica and hear the opinion of the friars, especially of Father Stjepan, who is disappointed and dismayed by what the Muslims have been doing. Insist on the complete withdrawal from Zenica, that is, Croats to move completely out of Zenica. We have learned that the Muslims are about to launch an attack of Zepce in five days. We are completely cut off from the world, but we have enough reserves to be able to take on and fight either one or the other." I'm going to ask you several questions about this, but I'm going to start from the bottom. First of all, I would like you to tell me whether this is an authentic copy of the original that was drafted by Ivo Livancic of the 11th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They say they are cut off completely from the world, but they accept to take on either of the two sides. Who are either of the two sides? Who are one or the other side?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: We know that, in the municipality of Zepce, as early as 1992, the HVO had established positions against the army of the Republika Srpska. In this statement, one of the two sides would be the army of the Republika Srpska. The other side, based on the behaviour which was described at the top of the document, the BH army, and the uncertainty as to their further actions, the other side would be the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Then it states: "We are completely cut off from the world".

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. Zepce was another enclave, just like the Lasva River Valley. They were completely cut off and they were surrounded by two armies, the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska, as was the HVO in the Lasva River Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that the reason why they are sending this report out to so many addressees, to General Petkovic, without really observing the proper chain of command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That is true. The commander of the 111th Brigade was forced to address the Chief of Staff of the Croatian Defence Council in Mostar and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna Defence Minister, as well as the Central Bosnia Operative Zone Commander because of the situation in his sector. He can foresee a very difficult situation; therefore, he is asking for assistance and instructions what to do in this type of situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this upset the usual way in which these reports should be sent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I said that the 111th Brigade was under the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. In terms of establishment and formation, it was subordinate to him. But because of the inability of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone to provide any assistance to the 111th Brigade, this commander, who was also commander of this Operative Group, addressed this report directly to the Chief of Staff and the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me take you to the third paragraph: "I am considering issuing an order on the withdrawal of our forces from the territory of the defence of the town of Maglaj, as a warning for the attacks they are conducting against our forces in Central Bosnia." Who was defending from whom and who would be warned? What kind of a warning would this be?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The positions and lines against the Bosnian Serb army near Maglaj were held by the HVO. The commander of the 111th Brigade, probably by following the media and monitoring the developments in his area, saw how fierce the attacks were against the Lasva River Valley conducted by the Bosnian army. He probably knew that the HVO troops had been driven out of Zenica and there were none left in Zenica. He may know that the HVO has been holding the lines against the Serbian army troops. So he is probably considering all of these elements, and he is trying to tie up the forces of the BH army in order to force them to take up positions against the Serbian army units. In that way, it would alleviate the pressure against the HVO positions in the Lasva River Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When somebody says, "I am considering," he says that he's considering withdrawing some troops from certain positions, does that not sound like self-will, which is not a very military approach to things?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Given the conflict in January of 1993 between the HVO and the BH army, we, in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, were unable to issue commands to this brigade in a way which was envisaged in military terms. It was an independent unit, and this is reflected by him saying, "I am considering," because he knew what his capabilities were in the area in which he operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D323, D323A for the French version, and D323B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we were viewing reports from Kiseljak on the 18th of April when the conflicts in Kiseljak started. On the basis of Blaskic's report of the 17th, addressed to the brigade in Kiseljak, we now have a report of the Kiseljak Brigade, Ban Jelacic, dated the 19th of April, 1993. It is addressed to the command of the Operative Zone, and it says: "1) Enemies: Chetniks: No combat activities in the brigade's zone of responsibility. In Koscan, there is a lull in the fighting. Muslim armed forces continue to fire from infantry weapons on our positions from the region of Gomionica. They attempted a counterattack from Gomionica village which we have repelled. In the Podbrdja region, the Muslim armed forces fired at our forces. 2) Our forces: Our forces continue with intensive activities in the Gomionica village, since the MOS attempted a counterattack. They are trying to reinforce their positions along the lines they have reached. In other parts of the municipality, there is a lull. 3) Suggestions: None. 4) Requests: Inform us of the current situation in Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Operations Officer on Duty, Mato Lucic." First, Brigadier, do you remember this report? Do you recognise the stamps and the contents?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do recall the contents because we had a keen interest in developments in the area of Gomionica because it is visible from this report how fierce the fighting there was. The report reached the communications centre. Mato Lucic was an officer on duty in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D324, D324A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, again, we have a rather poor copy, but I shall try to read out the key sentences, but not the whole document, because I don't consider it to be necessary because we already know where the forces were deployed. This is a report by the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski from Busovaca dated the 19th of April. The hour is not indicated. The text reads: "On the 19th of April, 1993 at 0645 hours, a general attack began on Busovaca from the direction of Dvor-Putis-Gradina. Grid reference point 650. It is believed that this was done by parts of the 7th Muslim Brigade from Zenica, up to 500 men strong, armed with automatic weapons. The probable aim of the attack is to capture the grid reference point 650 and hold the surrounding villages under control. The Solakovici-Milavice attack was carried out by parts of the 333rd Brigade from Busovaca and the 309th Mountain Brigade from Kakanj, 450 men strong, with the aim of pushing back our forces from the areas under our control. The Kapak-Polom-Ocehnici attack was carried out by parts of the 333rd Mountain Brigade from Busovaca and 302nd Brigade from Visoko, 400 men strong, with the aim of capturing the predominant features and the Draga barracks. On the axis Dusina-Lasva-Merdani-Grablje, forces are stationed from the 305th Jajce Brigade and portions of the 303rd Mountain Brigade and the 301st Motorised Brigade from Zenica. The said forces are probably in reserve and will be acting on the axis Lasva-Merdani and the road Lasva-Grablje-Kaonik, with the aim of taking control of the lines we are holding and controlling communications. These forces are 2.000 men strong, and the 301st Motorised Mountain Brigade also has some tanks so the use of the same cannot be ruled out. In the last sentence, Dusko Grubisic, the commander says: "At the moment, there are about 1.300 soldiers engaged, including support in personnel added to us from other units." Brigadier, first, do you recall the contents of this report?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do. This was the strongest attack by BH army units in the area of Busovaca municipality in the period from the 16th to the 19th of April, 1993. The report reached us from the Busovaca Brigade. It was received in the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this a faithful copy of the original that you received?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. The underlining in the original was done by me because I was studying this report to get an idea of the situation on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D325, D325A for the French version, D325B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we are now looking at document D325, which is actually a report of the Viteska Brigade, also on the 19th of April, but at 600 hours. It is addressed to you in the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The text reads: "Last night, Muslim forces from the Lokve region shelled parts of the Kruscica settlement which is under our control. Six mortar shells fell. Two private houses were hit, one Muslim and one Croat. There were no casualties." The third paragraph says: "Additional mobilisation of personnel has been carried out and new trenches and reinforcements are continuously being created along the defence lines. We are doing everything possible to secure the possibility of the Novi Travnik-Vitez-Busovaca road, because it is certain that the enemy will try everything to intercept this communication in certain places. Fatigue can be observed among our soldiers. We are trying to give them the opportunity to rest and prepare for the decisive battle." Brigadier, do you remember the contents of this report?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do. The report was written in the Viteska Brigade, and it was received in the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The stamp confirming receipt, is it an original one of the command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D326, D326A for the French version, D326B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document is a report of the head of the medical department, Dr. Drago Dzambas, who, on the 19th of April at 1600 hours, is submitting a report to the main medical corps headquarters. "Since 17 April (from 1100 hours) until today, 19 April (1630 hours)," so this is a period that is just over 48 hours long. I don't want to read the text, but I would like to read a part from the second paragraph. "In the Nova Bila war hospital (Franciscan Hospital) which is being used as the collection and selection point, between the last report and the present, we have had 50 new casualties (altogether since the beginning until today there have been 100 casualties), out of which there were three new deaths in the hospital. The number of soldiers and civilians killed on the territory of Central Bosnia is about 60 to 65. As we are under siege and being tapped, we are protesting and appealing for assistance from the International Community due to the brutal attack by the Muslim fundamentalists on villages and the civilian population. Chief of the Medical Corps, Dr. Drago Dzambas." Brigadier, did the Chief of the Medical Corps address such a report to the main headquarters of the medical corps in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I remember this report because it reached us also in the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These numbers, that is, 60 to 65 dead and 100 wounded in three days of fighting, are they correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I cannot claim with 100 per cent certainty that those figures are correct, but if it was written by Dr. Dzambas, who kept records of those figures, I believe they are correct. However, Mr. President, Your Honours, I should like to focus on the sentence which says: "The collection and selection war hospital in Nova Bila." The HVO and the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Colonel Blaskic, not only did he have problems in defending the defence lines, as shown in the municipality of Vitez and Busovaca, but, also, we didn't have a medical institution to provide proper treatment to our wounded. Instead, we improvised a hospital in a church in Nova Bila and, with the help of doctors from medical institutions in the Lasva Valley, we provided treatment from this date throughout the war until the Washington Agreement. We treated the wounded in such an improvised hospital. For this reason, we see such an appeal, such a request, by the Chief of the Medical Corps to his superiors in the profession in the health department of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna for aid. A second point I wish to make is the statement by the doctor himself, and that is that our reports and links and communications with our main headquarters in Prosje were being tapped, so that some reports that we send there had to be put in such a way as to present the situation in a better light than they really were so that the enemy would not have the proper information to inflict the final blow on us and our defence lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. Let us now go on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D326, D326A for the French version, D326B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. It is 327. The interpreter made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the transcript, it is D327, D327A for the French version, D327B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, another poor copy, but I shall do my best to read it, some of the important parts. D327 is a report of the Viteska Brigade on the 19th of April, 1993 to the command of the Operative Zone. It says in the first paragraph: "During the whole day, intensive attacks continued by Muslim forces on HVO units and civilian facilities and villages populated by Croats. All lines of defence from the previous report are still under control with additional efforts from personnel and equipment. Very heavy fighting went on in the vicinity of Sivrino Selo village." Then I will go on to the next paragraph: "At 1600 hours, from the region of Vjetrenica, probably from the saddle Vjetrenica-Kuber, Muslim forces shelled from a tank (probably T-34) the town of Vitez itself. The municipality building was hit and the aggressor was probably targeting also the post office, the hotel, the Workers' University, as well as civilian buildings in town. Apart from material damage, there was no other consequences." Something is written by hand, but I can't read it. "Enemy snipers are still active in the town, firing at anything that moves," and then hand-written, "especially women and children." Then the second paragraph from the bottom: "We are short of 7.9 and 9 millimetre ammunition. Last night, on the 18th of April, 1993 in the suburb of Grbavica, Muslim extremists detained the remaining Croatian citizens and took them in an unknown direction." Then those arrested are listed, and the document is signed by the operations officer on duty. Do you recall this document from the 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the contents, especially the shelling of the municipality building and the other buildings listed in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell us, this tank, how did the appearance of a tank affect the population, in view of the fact that you mostly had small arms?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The appearance of a tank, under our conditions, really did cause panic and fear and caused disorganisation in an already disorganised situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D328, D328A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before going onto this document, D328, could we summarise on this map, to the best of your recollection and on the basis of the reports, where the conflicts occurred on the 19th of April? This is a document referring to the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, on the 19th of April 1993, on the basis of the reports we received from the Viteska Brigade and the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade from Busovaca, the fiercest conflicts and the fiercest attacks by BH army units were in the following localities within the territory of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, I want to understand well. Are we talking about the 19th or the 20th of April? The report says the 19th, and the situation is the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are talking about the 19th of April. So I would prefer the maps to be distributed first so each of Your Honours has a map before him, and the next report, which has already been given a number, will be dealing with the 20th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be a better idea. You don't have to change the numbering, Mr. Registrar, but it would be better if we could be given a map, as we had before, for the various dates.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D320, the number of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the map should be 321. The 320 exhibit, as I understand it, is the photograph taken of the scale model with the flags.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, 320 is the photograph of the scale model, and 321 is the map for the 19th of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, the map has a number, D321, and looking at that map, and pointing to the screen with your pointer, can you indicate the places of conflict on the 19th of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, let me repeat, the places of conflict and shelling were marked on the basis of reports we received from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, from Busovaca, and the Viteska Brigade. The small circle indicates the broader area of infantry conflicts, and the arrow indicates the places that was heavily shelled during the day. Let me indicate the places of conflict within the territory of Busovaca municipality. The fiercest conflicts and the fiercest attacks by the BH army were in the surroundings of Prosje, Ocehici, Ocehnici, Milavici, in the area of Putis, Gradina. Those were the localities within the territory of Busovaca. As for attacks in the Vitez municipality, the fiercest attacks were, as we learned from the reports, was Sivrino Selo, Pirici and Santici. Here, we see the name Pirici. The shelling on the same day, heavy shelling that went on throughout the day, were particularly fierce in the following places in Busovaca municipality. First, the town of Busovaca itself, and the separation line, or the line of separation between the Busovaca and Viteska Brigade, that is the area of Kratine, the slopes of Mount Kuber, then the area of Santici, the area of Donja Dubravica, the town of Vitez itself, the defended parts of the village of Kruscica, that is, the part of the village where HVO units were located. The area of Krcevine, a village defended by HVO units, and the area of the village of Jardo. All these localities that were being shelled, if we were to compare them with the scale model, we can see that positions are being shelled of the HVO units which are defending Croatian villages within the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca, as well as the towns of Busovaca and Vitez, themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. So, we have completed a brief review of events on the 19th of April 1993. We have before us the document number D328. It is the first document relating to the 20th of April, 1993, which reached us from the command of the Travnik Brigade. This is extraordinary combat report, I would like to review it. In item one it states: "In the Travnik town proper, from the barracks up to the entry into town, from the direction of Vitez, Muslim forces are arresting Croats on a mass scale, and they are also taking them away. So far the following people have been taken away. Andrija Eldic was released, Zeljo Glogoski, Anto Sakota, Mario Solumun, Anto Volic and Ilija Martinovic, and we have information that Mrs. Zvonke Gase was killed in her apartment. According to the latest information our communications are tapped. In the Kalibunar area we have difficulties in controlling our forces." And the rest is not important, and the operative on duty, Ljupko Kozina. Do you recall this information from 20 April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall it. I especially recall it regarding the murder of Mrs. Zvonke Gase, which at that time was just presumed, but then it turned out to be true. She was the wife of one of the commanders of the Viteska Brigade. All the others here were in the town of Travnik. And as I pointed out on the scale map, in Travnik and Novi Travnik there was no fighting. However, you can see a situation which, for all intents and purposes, is like having a conflict in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this tapping of communication lines something that was usual, there in item two?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. In all command posts we knew that the BH army units had capabilities of eavesdropping, and they were on the surrounding hills and we were down in the valley. And given the technical equipment, there was always a possibility, and there were actual instances where we were tapped. And so, these reports are very short and incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am told by my client that Madam Zvonke Gase was killed, and she was the wife of one of the commanders of the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the husband of Mrs. Zvonke Gase was a member of the Travnik Brigade, not the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D329, D329A for the French version, D329B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a document from the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command on 20 April 1993 at 1115 hours, and it is titled "The mutual cessation of hostilities." It has a number of addressees, it is to the commanders of the brigades one through twelve, the independent units in the Operative Zone, the Chief of the HVO main headquarters and the A BH army, 3rd Corps, and European Community Monitoring Commission. This is the text. "On the basis of a joint order by the chief of the HVO main headquarters and the chief of the A BH main headquarters, and in connection with a bilateral cease-fire, I hereby order: 1) All HVO units in the area of responsibility of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone immediately cease fire and hostilities against the A BiH units. 2) Do not open fire in response to sporadic shooting by the A BiH units. 3) In the case of an open attack and heavy firing at the HVO units, return fire energetically and prevent a breakthrough. 4) Acquaint all units under your command in your area of responsibility with this order. This order shall come into effect on 20 April 1993 at 1900 hours and the commanders of the brigades and of the independent units are personally responsible to me for its execution. Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recognise this document. I personally drafted it, it was signed by the commander of the Operative Zone, Colonel Blaskic. It was created on the basis of agreement between the HVO main headquarters and the BiH army headquarters in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, Brigadier, we're not going to comment on this document any further. I would like to move on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 330, D330A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this document of the 20 of April is from the Vitez Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please go ahead, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the original which I have before me, I cannot see it very well, but the translators were apparently able to decipher the entire sentence. But I'm going to move on to the second sentence, which may be the more relevant one. "In the evening of 19 April 1993, from the direction of the village of Gacice the enemy fired, most probably with the recoilless gun, BTS," I believe?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is a recoilless gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, the 82 millimetre recoilless gun "three projectiles on the command post of the Viteska Brigade. There were no casualties, only material damage. Currently fighting is in progress around the village of Gacice, where several sniper nests are located, paralysing almost entirely the centre of town. During the night the Muslims more probably regrouped their forces and started the attacks in the early morning. An attack was carried out yesterday evening against our forces in Zabrde. The mountain lodge was set on fire, and according to unconfirmed reports, some of our men were killed. We assumed the attack was carried out by the Muslim units from Kruscica in cooperation with those from Novi Travnik". And in parentheses it says "Opara". "Our forces are on the defence lines and one 50-man unit was sent to Zabrde to recapture this feature. The action is running according to plan and with satisfactory speed". And then the last part is again barely legible but I'll try to read it: "On the premises of the Viteska Brigade command, prominent representatives of Muslims gathered during the night with the goal of finding a way to stop the armed conflict. Together with the representatives of the HVO Vitez government, certain conclusions were reached, and a copy is," I guess it says "attached", or "enclosed". Brigadier, do you recall these events around the village of Gacice, and what do you recall?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do recall the events in Gacice and the mountain lodge in Zabrde, I also recall that. In the village of Gacice, which is a village where the population was mixed, the Croatian and Muslim Bosnia population, and there were both the BH army units there and the HVO units. Those were not big forces. And on this particular day I know that a conflict broke out and the HVO units pushed back the BH army units, and as far as I know, they pushed them back in the direction of Kruscica. I also recall this combat operation at Zabrde. I could also show it on the scale model, in order to provide a better picture about the efforts of the BH army to continue their strangle hold, and to reduce the amount of ground held by the HVO to a minimum.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, Brigadier. Before that, is this a true copy of the original which you had received?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Regarding the events which I have just related, I recall it as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the scale model, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the location from where BH army units arrived and carried out the attack at Zabrde, part of the movement was across the mountain paths and then the villages of Trenza (phoen), Cakice (phoen), and the lateral roads which have not been entered here. And they attacked the Zabrde; and our units, which were there, were pushed from these positions, and the town of Vitez and the villages controlled by the HVO were further threatened in terms of their tactical situation. Because the town of Vitez and the surrounding villages were almost like on the palm of your hand, you could see exactly any movement, who was moving and where they were moving. And if you had appropriate weapons, you could control all these roads and the entire area under the HVO control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you show the village of Gacice, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. This is Ocice. The village of Gacice is situated here. And this is where the units of the BH army and HVO clashed. The HVO units pushed the BH army back, and this is how I marked them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, if you are more or less finished with the presentation of these documents and the use of the scale model, I propose a 15 or 20-minute break. We now stand in recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us now resume with the hearing. Would the registrar please bring the accused back in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We'll have another 15-minute break at around 5.15 or so, and then we will continue until 6.15, 6.30.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D331A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is the Viteska Brigade command, 20 April, 1993 at 1800 hours, Operations Report: "Heavy attacks on the HVO units by Muslim forces continued throughout the afternoon. Infantry breakthroughs were attempted on several occasions on lines in the Krcevine and Krizancevo Selo regions. At the moment, fierce battles are being waged in Krizancevo Selo where the Mujahedeen forces have already descended. The Croatian population are panicking and have started fleeing from their homes. We are attempting to stabilise the situation and the defence is focusing now on Dubravica. The BH army forces are attacking our units from several directions: From the Bukve-Ljubici and Slatine axis on Krcevine, and from the Tolovici position on Krizancevo Selo and Dubravica. An attack on Zabrde is expected. The Gacice village is 100 per cent completed. Forty-seven men were taken prisoner. Women and children were sent home. Snipers are still attacking the town and the defence lines. We had four soldiers killed in today's fighting (one from Novi Travnik) and four wounded." Brigadier, do you recall the facts from this report on 20 April, 1993 which arrived in your command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I do recall the facts which are referred to in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There is no incoming stamp here at your communications centre; why?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As I already stated, some messages were coming by courier where it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D332, D332A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Another report, this time from the Busovaca Brigade, same date, 20 April, and the situation is as of 2200 hours, and that is when it reached your command centre. I'll read the body of text: "Throughout the afternoon and evening, the aggression on our municipality continued. The attacks on the Poloma region continued. Our units repelled the attack and pushed the enemy back to its initial position. In the course of the battle, quite a few of our soldiers were killed and wounded. In the Roski Stijene area, our units also repelled the attack and pushed the Muslim forces back to their original positions. There were also killed and wounded soldiers in this battle. We have no official information about the number of soldiers killed and wounded, and we will send in a report later. Also, clashes in the Putis-Gradina-Jelinak area and in the Bara and Donje Rovne areas have resumed. Because of the difficult communications and radio systems, we have not received reports about the number of casualties. The defence lines are stable and the morale of soldiers and logistic support are satisfactory." Brigadier, did you receive this report on the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We received it through the packet communications. I do recall the events referred to in this report. From it, we see that the forces, which had been brought in to reinforce and in order to assist the attack in Busovaca, were used. These forces are attacking, and we see what the situation is in the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski at that given hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you often hear verbally or in written form? "Because of the written communications, we have not received reports about the number of casualties." In other words, the difficulties you experienced in communicating, we know how the situation was with the command, but what was the situation within the brigade itself, let's say, from the brigade down to the battalion, from the battalion down to the company, and so on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The farther down the chain you went, from battalion to company, to platoon, and squad, the communication system was poorer and poorer, because we did not have enough equipment to cover all these formations. The level of platoons and squads, as far as I recall within the brigades, all communications were done by courier. Therefore, the reports to the commander of the brigade were also coming in late.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let me point you to the hour here. It says "2200 hours," whereas you received it on 21 April at 0100 hours. In other words, three hours later you received this report. This is the brigade which is located within the enclave. Did the command have any communications in real time? In military terms, what is "real time"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Because of the poor level of communications, the Operative Zone command never had the factual picture or situation in real time. The real time would be the time, for instance, when you would receive an information about something at the time when something occurred. This is a report on something that took place throughout this day and as of 2200 hours of that day, anything that happened on that day up to 2200 hours, even though this report came to us at 0157 hours on the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In modern warfare, is the real time the only time that is counted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that the real time is when the information is received immediately upon an event taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D333, D333A for the French version, and D333B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we have an order of Brigadier Petkovic, the Chief of Staff of the Main Headquarters, which was sent at different times, we see those times, to different operative zones, to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone at 0320. It states: "In connection with the rights and obligations of the Red Cross (ICRC) which follow from the Geneva Agreements of 22 May and 6 June, 1992, and in view of the recent developments in relations between the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO, that is, the possibility that combat activities and emotional stress may cause disrespect for and violations of the rights of the ICRC and of all others who are included in the Geneva Agreement and in the spirit of the orders issued to date, I hereby order: 1) Make sure the ICRC has free access to civilians in all areas. 2) Respect and protect the civilian population affected by combat operations. 3) Treat captured civilians and soldiers in a humane fashion and provide them with adequate protection. 4) Report the identity of all captured or imprisoned persons to the ICRC and allow their representatives to visit them. 5) Round up, care for, and protect all wounded persons everywhere and at all times, regardless of which side they belong to. 6) Allow free access and passage to humanitarian aid and medical convoys. 7) Once again, familiarise all units under your command with this order. Chief Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic," signed of the main headquarters. Brigadier, did you receive such an order on 20 April at the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. We did receive it. I do remember it, and I recall also that we issued an appropriate order in compliance with this order to our subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that this order speaks for itself, and I would just like to move on to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D334, D334A for the French version, D334B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm reading the document D334. The command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia on the 21st of April, 1993 issues an order to HVO brigades from 1 to 12, independent units, the 4th Military Police Battalion, and the Special Purposes Unit Vitezovi, Vitez. The order issued by Colonel Blaskic reads: "On the basis of the command of the chief of staff of the HVO main headquarters," then in black ink, the same as was used for indicating the reference number, "01-4-444/93, further to the exercise of the rights and duties of the International Red Cross, as stipulated in the Geneva Agreements of 22 May to 6 June, 1992, and with regard to the recent developments in relations between the HVO and the BH army, that is, violations of the rights of the International Red Cross and all others covered by the Geneva Agreement caused by combat activities and emotional stress, and in the spirit of the recent orders, I hereby order: 1) Allow the ICRC free access to the civilians in all areas. 2) Respect and protect the civilian population caught up in combat activities. 3) Treat the captured civilians and soldiers humanely and provide them with suitable protection. 4) Report the identity of all prisoners and detainees to the ICRC and allow ICRC representatives to visit them. 6) Allow free access and passage to convoys of humanitarian aid. 7) Inform all units under your command of this order." Brigadier, even though this order is a very, very poor copy that we have, do you recall this order as written?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do. I wrote it myself. It was signed by General Blaskic. The corrections in it were done by General Blaskic the moment I gave him the document to sign. This is the order that I mentioned when talking about the order of the main headquarters that was addressed to subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We notice a complete correspondence, to the letter, to the word, between this order and the order of General Petkovic. Was that typical of Colonel Blaskic, to respect orders, or was he prone to improvise and give his own interpretations to superior orders? What kind of an officer was he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: General Blaskic, in my view, was a highly professional commander, and it was his principle and his style of work to observe, to the letter, superior commands. Any commands coming from the main headquarters, he sought to implement them fully. This order confirms this characteristic of General Blaskic's. May I also add, in this connection, my own personal impressions of the General when I was working with him throughout the war in those difficult times? General Blaskic had such a civilised behaviour. We would spend hours and hours together in the most difficult circumstances, and he never addressed me, his closest associate, in any other way but as "Mr. So-and-so," and that was the way he addressed all his subordinates, and I wondered why he did so. This was due to the fact that General Blaskic was fully aware of his ultimate and only goal, and that is to establish an organisation of the HVO. And in order to achieve that, as he wanted to, he wanted to set a personal example to show what a professional attitude of an officer should be within an institution under your command. Mr. President, Your Honours, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, interpersonal relations, regardless of status, duty, and position, a person in Bosnia after meeting you, after a couple of sentences, will address you in the familiar manner. He will start using this familiar tone. This, too, was a reason why General Blaskic wanted to set a personal example and, through us, to influence his subordinate commanders, so that in the HVO relations of subordination, superiority should be established so that people would know exactly what to do when they received orders from a superior. However, he was working under circumstances, which we have been discussing for the past four or five days, so we know the kind of conditions that we were working in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. We have a new document, now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D335, D335A for the French version, 335B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we now have a report or a note obviously written by Colonel Blaskic after a meeting with the chief of the main command, Sefer Halilovic, and the Chief of Staff of the main command of the HVO. So, the Supreme Commander of the BiH army and of the HVO. Also present, among others, was Blaskic, and the meeting was chaired by Ambassador Thebault. We will not read the whole text, because it is lengthy, although I consider it to be extremely relevant and important because it speaks of the positions of the BH army and the positions of the HVO. But I would like to focus on the last part, where it says: "Other observations". So, could you please try and refresh your memory of that day when he came back from the meeting, and what he told you, and what was happening? "Other observations:" And this is what Blaskic writes in his report on the last page. "1. A large number of civilian casualties. 2. The delegation of the BH army is worried and cold and distant. 3. Total lack of attention to essential problems, their answer to everything is no problems. 4. Vehbija is preoccupied, his thoughts are elsewhere, he takes notes, follows everything said, but is full of hatred. 5. Siber is a commander of the BH army, behaves as if he had known me. 6. Merdan, deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, he keeps inventing one-sided reasons for the conflict, is pretty worried about the 500 civilians killed in Vitez. 7. I'm said to be good if Kordic was not giving me orders, and that is a big problem for everyone. 8. My personal impression is they are either totally scatterbrained, so they have agreed to everything, or they can no longer control their own actions so now they accept everything in order to create space for a new attack, one they will not give up on." Brigadier, are you aware of these notes from the meeting? And do you know that Blaskic wrote it and signed it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the content of the note on the meeting. This is not General Blaskic's signature, I cannot exactly remember whose signature it is, but it does bear the stamp of the Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let this document be a basis for refreshing your memory. Do you remember that Blaskic went to Zenica to attend a meeting with the BH army to negotiate a cease-fire? Do you remember what he told you when he came back, what they had discussed at the meeting, what did he learn at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do, indeed, remember that day very well. The meeting in Zenica was held in order to carry out the order on the cessation of hostilities between units of the BH and the HVO, addressed by the main headquarters, that is Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic and the Chief of Staff of the BH army. I remember precisely when General Blaskic left for that meeting in Zenica. He left in the organisation of UNPROFOR. And in the operative centre, I stayed behind, my task being to be in touch with him and to coordinate all activities between our command and our subordinate units. I remember that day in particular, because something occurred which should not have occurred, especially not something that was done by the army, even though it had signed the cease-fire. This was in the evening, it was already dark, and in my assessment, I think that General Blaskic must have already reached the place of the meeting; but I was told by the Viteska Brigade that a strong attack had been launched by BH army units from Dubravica towards the road and the railway station in Vitez. Let me show you with this pointer. It is this direction (indicating). And in this attack the BH army units reached ten metres away from the road. There was panic, they called up from the Viteska Brigade because they received orders on a cessation of fire. People had relaxed after four days of heavy fighting, and the command of that BH army unit took advantage of the moment. In my view this was a planned action, it was a fierce attack; but investing extreme effort, the BH army units were pushed back to initial positions. What did I do? I called up the command of the 3rd Corps, luckily I managed to get through. I asked to talk to General Blaskic, I informed him of the same and told him to ask the commander of the 3rd Corps to cease such activities. At that time, and there were several similar incidents, the power was cut off in Vitez and the town was in total darkness. We in the command were not ready for this, and we sought a way of providing electric light to be able to continue working, and I informed General Blaskic of this. He intervened with the commander of the 3rd Corps; but my personal conclusion is that the HVO units, had they not managed to push back BH army units to initial positions, regardless of the order issued to respect the cease-fire and to cease hostilities, the BH army units would have cut across this road over which we had fought throughout the war. These are some events that remain clear in my mind during the time that General Blaskic was in Zenica. I shall now go onto General Blaskic's return from Zenica. I have already said that I actually met him during the war. So I noticed on his face that he was worried and depressed, and he uttered only one sentence, and I shall try to remember it fully. "I have been informed that in the conflicts, in the territory of the Vitez municipality, and especially in Ahmici, there were a large number of people killed, among whom there are civilians." That was the information he conveyed, and it was then that I learned that in Ahmici a large number of people had been killed, among whom there were civilians. As for the other matters discussed, I learned about them from the report, and after this statement by General Blaskic, because of his overall attitude and the way he looked to me, I didn't ask anything more about this meeting, because he told me that there would be a complete report, and that is the report that we have before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, Brigadier, there were two meetings at the time, one in Zenica, one in Bila; do you recall both meetings or only the one in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do not recall the meeting in Bila very well, because I was preoccupied with the events I have just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go on to the next document, it is another order by Blaskic dated the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D336, D336A for the French version, 336B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Before proceeding to the next document, I should just like clarification to be made. In comments on the document 335A in French, under number 6, it says "Merdan is very worried about the 500 civilians killed in Vitez." Are those Bosniaks, Croats, those civilians? What kind of civilians were they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I cannot provide a precise answer to this question, because I don't know what was implied by this sentence, because there were dead civilians both among the Croats and the Muslim Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But according to your recollection, is this a realistic figure, even if we added both Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I think that the figure is nowhere near a realistic one, according to what I learned subsequently about the actual losses and casualties, both within HVO ranks and BH army ranks, and the victims among the Croatian population and the Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you are implying this is an exaggeration?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is my impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document is D336. It is an order by Colonel Blaskic issued on the 21st of April 1993 at 0910 hours. The heading is "Implementation of the agreement between units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO. Order: On the 21st of April 1993, at 1200 hours, a meeting was held in Nova Bila between the Chief of Staff of the main headquarters of the HVO and the chief of the main headquarters of the BH army. On the basis of the agreement reached between Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic and Chief of the main command of the BH army, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, and with the objective of implementing it fully, I hereby order: First: Halt all combat activities against BH army units and commence securing installations, positions, settlements and communications; also, increase the control of the territory. Responsible, the immediate subordinated commanders. Deadline, immediately. I forbid the opening of fire in the event of provocations on the part of the BiH army soldiers. Combat activities may be carried out only in the event of provocations and open attacks by BH army units and in strict compliance with the orders of the superior commander. Responsible: The immediately subordinated commanders, defence sector commanders. Deadline: Immediately. 4) Ensure unfettered movement of U.N. forces and European Community Monitoring Mission team along all roads in the zone of responsibility in the HVO command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and according to previously submitted orders. Responsible: Commanders of HVO brigades, commander of the military police of the HVO in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. Deadline: Immediately. 5) In the period agreed, simultaneous with the withdrawal of the BH army forces, withdraw all military units from the Sljivcica-Vrhovin and Gavrine Kuce lines; whereas, the area Kaonik Zenica to the right and Vjetrenica Zenica to the left, along the Vitez Kaonik road in the depth of the Zenica area remains a demilitarised area occupied by U.N. forces only, free of military units. 6) HVO brigade commanders are obliged to guarantee full security to Muslim civilians and other civilians in the area of responsibility. Competent HVO authorities are duty bound to ensure public law and order, especially with regard to the Muslim inhabitants of the town of Vitez and the Croatian inhabitants of the town of Zenica. I hereby appoint the following people to a joint coordination team: Mr. Franjo Nakic, chief of the HVO staff; Mr. Zoran Pilicic, member of the Operative Zone command; and Mr. Vukovic. The joint team will commence with its work on the 22nd of April 1993 at 1000 hours in Nova Bila in the ECMM headquarters. 8) Brigade commanders are obliged to issue written orders to their subordinate commanders on the basis of this order and to start implementing it. They are to send one copy of their order to the Vitez Operative Zone Central Bosnia command. 9) Immediately subordinate commanders are personally responsible to me for the full execution of this order." Signed "Colonel Blaskic". Tell us, Brigadier, do you remember this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do, or rather, I recall the content, because I had the same in my hands, I was partly responsible for its implementation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. The text speaks for itself, so we can proceed to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D337, D337A for the French version, 337B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we received this document from the Prosecutor's office. It is hand-written in English, so the original document is in English, so I would like to ask my colleague, Mr. Hayman, to read it. My colleague is telling me that there is a Croatian version, so I will read it after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, the document was issued by the 3rd Corps of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, on the 22nd of April, 1993. And it says: "Based on the agreement to establish a joint operational centre at the level of the BH army 3rd Corps and the HVO headquarters of Central Bosnia, as the first step in order to establish the joint headquarters in regard to implementation of the said agreement, we are hereby appointing the following commission for dealing with all the problems and tasks in implementation of this agreement." Now we see three members on behalf of the BH army and three on behalf of the HVO, Hadzihasanovic has signed it, the commander of the 3rd Corps, and on behalf of the Operative Zone of Bosnia, Colonel Blaskic. Are you aware of this agreement and this document? There is another text underneath the names, it can hardly be read, and it says, roughly, "The appointed members of the commission are authorised to make all the necessary orders, instructions and tasks in accordance with the agreement signed." We received the document from the Prosecution, but regardless of that, will you tell us, Brigadier; is this Blaskic's signature and the stamp of the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, and I recall the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you tell us what was the purpose of creating a joint headquarters since there was a real war from the 16th to the 21st?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The purpose of this commission was to implement the tasks agreed at the meeting, and the ultimate task was to organise the HVO and the army for the battle against their common enemy, and that is the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D338, D338A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document is D338, it is a joint document of the command of the 3rd Corps in Zenica and the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. It was compiled in Bila on the 22nd of April 1993, and the heading is "The first joint operation centre of the Croatian Defence Council and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina" subtitle "Establishment of local commissions." "Order: Based on agreement reached between the chief of the main staff of the Croatian Defence Council and the chief of the general staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina under the chairmanship of General Morillon, U.N. force commander for Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Ambassador Thebault representing the European Community monitors, I order: 1) Local joint commissions composed of three members, representatives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO are to be established immediately in Vitez, Travnik, Busovaca and Kiseljak. 2) The composition of these joint local commissions, as well as the location where they will be established..." I can't see very well, "... should be reported in writing to the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and to the headquarters of the 3rd Corps. 3) The task of the joint commissions is to execute orders issued by the joint operations centre, which is located attached to the headquarters of the European Community Monitoring Mission in Bila, the municipality building in Vitez. 4) Local joint commissions shall supervise cessation of local hostilities and propose appropriate punishment against the violators to superior commanders of the Croatian Defence Council and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. 5) Each commission is under obligation to create conditions in which full security is guaranteed to the civilian population in its zone of responsibility, and the competent bodies have the duty to ensure public law and order. 6) Each commission shall undertake necessary measures in order to prevent arson, destruction and stealing of property owned by citizens within the area under its control. 7) Reporting. Until the establishment of communications between the operation centre in Bila and all local commissions, joint reports signed by both sides are to be sent to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and the 3rd Corps headquarters. Regular reports are to be sent daily by 2000 hours with the status as of 1900 hours, while special reports shall be sent as necessary." Signed by deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, Dzemo Merdan, and the stamp of the 3rd Corps; and the deputy commander of the HVO Operative Zone for Central Bosnia, Franjo Nakic, with the stamp of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Brigadier, do you recognise the stamp and signature of Mr. Nakic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do, as well as what has been hand-written, "ONO." It is a sign that the document reached me in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you can say that you actually saw this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, and I also remember the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please, because this one speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D339, D339A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let me read the document for you. It's numbered as 339, Defence Exhibit. This is in Mostar on 22 April, 1993, and "Done at Zenica, 20 April, 1993." The subject heading is "Agreement." "During the joint meeting held in Zenica, under the joint chairmanship of General Morillon, U.N. Force Commander for Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Mr. Thebault, Head of the EC Monitor Mission, the high level representatives agreed as follows: 1) The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO represent the legal defence forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and have equal treatment. 2) All commanders at all levels must observe and instantly establish a complete cease-fire on the entire territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, failure to observe a cease-fire is unacceptable under any circumstances. Both Chiefs of General Staff will immediately issue orders to fully observe a cease-fire. 3) A Joint Operations Centre has been established in Vitez at the level of the 3rd Corps of the BH army and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, as a first step in the establishment of a joint headquarters, which shall be set up in the course of the following days. At first, the Joint Operations Centre will be jointly led by both deputy commanders and representatives of brigades of both parties will participate as members. The Centre will be temporarily located in the current headquarters of the Busovaca Joint Commission in Vitez, which will enable close cooperation. UNPROFOR will provide all necessary assistance, particularly regarding security measures. At the same time, local joint commissions will be established at the brigade level to ensure full and immediate cooperation. The Joint Operations Centre will be established on Wednesday, 21 April, 1993 and will immediately begin to operate in the entire territory. The centre is authorised to issue joint orders which shall immediately be implemented in the field. The Chiefs of General Staff will meet on a weekly basis in order to ensure close and continuous cooperation on all relevant issues. These meetings shall be held alternately in Mostar and Zenica. The next meeting will be held in Mostar." Item 5 is not fully legible. On the next page, it says: "A joint report will be prepared daily by the Corps Commander and the commander of the Operative Zone in order to immediately inform both chiefs of staff." Then it says: "Chiefs of General Staff of the General Headquarters of the Army of BH, Sefer Halilovic; Chief of General Staff of the Croatian Defence Council at the General Headquarters, Milivoj Petkovic; U.N. Force Commander for BiH," and it's not fully legible. It must be "General Philippe Morillon." Then, "Head of the ECC Regional Centre." Again, I can't see it well. It must be "Jean-Pierre Thebault." Then, "Accuracy of transcription certified by Dobroslav Barbaric." Then we have a stamp of the communications centre of the main headquarters of the HVO. Do you recall the facts which are spelled out here in this document which was prepared in Zenica? In other words, following 20 April, did the facts of this agreement reach you in your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I partially remember this agreement. This agreement arrived in the Operative Zone command. As far as I understand it, this is a transcription of the text regarding the agreed-to activities from this meeting in Zenica between the HVO units and the BH army, represented by the Chief of Staff of the HVO, Milivoj Petkovic, and Sefer Halilovic, Chief of Staff of the BH army. We saw the further facts of this in previous reports. As far as the obligations of the HVO are concerned, we carried all of them out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, in your opinion, could it have happened that General Blaskic, in a way in which you met him, which was in a professional context, would not obey General Petkovic or anybody at such a high level?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No. That could not have happened and, in this particular case, it did not happen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is document D340.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have the original of the letter which General Blaskic sent to Robert Stewart, BRITBAT Commander. We received it from the Prosecution, and my colleague, Mr. Hayman, will be so kind as a read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "Vitez, April 23, 1993." The addressee is "UNPROFOR, Lieutenant Colonel Robert Stewart, BRITBAT Commander. 1) I am ready to send immediately the investigating commission to village of Ahmici as well as to all other places that need to investigated because of gathering facts about all the innocent victims this conflict. I, myself, beg you to help us stop this suffering and make the adequate conditions for the commission to work properly. As stated by both ABiH and HVO, everybody seems to be right, lles fighting is still going on, threatening to grow into the catastrophe and the disaster for all the people of this region. 2) I suggest that a new meeting is urgently summoned between the head of staff and the HVO head of staff, together with the commanders of HVO Operational Zone Middle Bosnia and the commander of the 3rd Corps, since I think it might prevent this from growing into even worse," and then perhaps the next word is "disaster," "which would be totally out of anybody's control. 3) I consider you to be an utterly honourable and professional soldier," it appears, "which gives me the cause to beg you as a man begs a man, please intervene in our further negotiations together with Mr. Thebault.
