Thankful in advance, with respect," and then I believe the indication is "for Colonel Tihomir Blaskic," although the signature, we'll have to ask the witness if he recognises it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let's see, do you recognise the signature and the stamp?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is my signature. I signed this document on behalf of General Blaskic by his authorisation, and it was done at the Operative Zone command, and it bears its stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When the commander issues you an order to draft such a document, does he give you any pointers? Why is he addressing Colonel Stewart?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: When we talked about this document and when he told me to sign it, and I do not recall exactly where he was at that moment, he must have been tied up somewhere, he told me that he wanted to ascertain the real facts regarding the death of civilians in the area of Vitez municipality, both Bosnians and Croats, and especially in the village of Ahmici. For that purpose, this particular letter was drafted, and it reflects exactly the instructions of General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, why couldn't he just go with the investigating commission to Ahmici and send this commission to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: He could not have sent this commission to Ahmici at that time, because the area of Ahmici, at that point, was still within the range of the small arms, the infantry weapons, of the positions of the BH army units. Because at the beginning of our hearing today, we mentioned those lines. This entire village was in a position where the small arms fire could be effectively used there. So these members of the commission could not carry out their duties as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, you said 5.15. We have just reached that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Let us now take a recess and return in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is now in session. Please have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, we're now going to continue. Judge Shahabuddeen has a question he would like to ask you, one question, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, we are dealing with a document signed by this witness and addressed to Lieutenant Colonel Robert Stewart. Would you help my recollection on the point as to whether Lieutenant Colonel Robert Stewart testified?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your Honour, Robert Stewart did not testify here. He was the British Battalion Commander in Central Bosnia during the events in Ahmici. However, the Prosecution did not call him as a witness in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That answers my failure in recall. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Otherwise, Robert Stewart is the man who brought all the media to Ahmici. He published a book on it. He is quite well-known. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you know, Bob Stewart, the U.N. commander in the area, did he accept the proposal of Blaskic to set up a joint commission in order to investigate? Did Bob Stewart accept such a proposal, on the basis of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as I recall, this proposal, which was sent by General Blaskic, commander of the Operative Zone, was not accepted by the commander of the British Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will show you another document which details what General Blaskic did regarding Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D341, D341A for the French version, D341B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document was received by the Defence from the Prosecution which came in a redacted form. There is a place where a person or a body, an institution, would have been indicated who was the addressee. This is the form in which we received the document. We did nothing with it in that regard, but let me read it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I just comment on that? This was given to us by the HVO authorities in the redacted form. So the redaction that is X-ed out here was not done by the Office of the Prosecutor, but was provided to us by the Bosnian Croats in this fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We have taken note of that. I suppose the day will come when we will all know exactly what was under that line. Perhaps the accused could tell us one day. There is, at least, someone who knows, I'm sure. Let us continue. Thank you, Mr. Kehoe, for clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In any event, we all agree that none of us present here had redacted it, but it has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is addressed to the command of Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The date is 10 May, 1993; time, 1705 hours. It is addressed to the currently unknown addressee, and the subject heading is "Enquiry and Written Report on the Events in the Village of Ahmici. Order: For several days, various rumours have been circulating in the public regarding the events in the village of Ahmici since 14 May, 1993 and the civilian casualties there. In order to be able to analyse the events, establish the facts of the case and implement the order of the HVO Chief of Staff, I hereby issue the following order: 1) Gather all the information and submit a report on the events that actually took place in the village of Ahmici, in particular, on the number of casualties, the manner in which they occurred, and the perpetrators. 2) I designate the assistant for SIS, Security and Information Service, of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone as the person responsible for this task. The deadline is 25 May, 1993. Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, is this Colonel Blaskic's signature and is this the stamp of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is the signature of General Blaskic and the stamp of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were you in any manner involved in the investigation of the way it is put here, "events in the village of Ahmici"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In the duty which I had at the time, I had, I was not tasked to get involved in any investigations, nor did I take part in any manner in the events of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D342, document 342A for the French version and document D342B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "Croatian defensive council, security information service, the forward command post in Vitez. It is defence military secrets, strictly confidential, in the hands of the commander of the Central Operative Zone, Vitez, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. Subject: Information submitted." And the body of the text runs as follows. "As file enclosure, we submit to you information about the events in the village of Ahmici, Vitez municipality. This information encompasses operative findings and eyewitness accounts of these events, as well as an on-the-spot review of the site. The information is not complete and the case has not been fully resolved, because in these areas combat activities continue to take place and it was not possible to take written statements from several key eyewitnesses to the events. Also, statements were not taken from persons of Muslim nationality who, after the events in the village of Ahmici, fled to the municipality of Zenica, Travnik and elsewhere. In this respect an adequate collaboration of the opposite side was also missing for the completion of this case. After this cessation of combat activities and creation of more favourable conditions, all necessary measures and actions will be taken in order to shed light on this case fully." And then, deputy, assistant commander for the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No, did I not see it, it went directly to the commander. As I told you, this was not my area of work, that is the investigating work. But I do know Anto Sliskovic, assistant commander to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone commander, and I recognise his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D343, document D343A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps there may be a clarification regarding the previous document. This is the document D342. It says that there was an enclosure regarding the events in Ahmici; however, the Defence is not in possession of that enclosure. However, Colonel Blaskic was not satisfied with this, and he issued a new order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is dated 17 August 1993, time 1045, and it is assistant for SIS, attention is Mr. Anto Sliskovic, and it has to do with the continued investigation regarding killings in the village of Ahmici. "Order: In order to provide all the facts and take steps in further investigation in connection with the killing of the civilians in the village of Ahmici, I hereby order: 1) Continue with gathering data and collecting information considering the civilian casualties in the village of Ahmici in order to unify all the materials and provide the bodies of district military court that are in charge of those materials. 2) In gathering information pay special attention to such information which are of most relevance to the entire investigation. 3) The deadline for carrying out this order is 17 September 1993, at which time a complete report shall be sent to me in order to proceed with further procedure before the competent body. Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, who signed this order, and whose stamp is this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: From the initials in the corner, it is clear that Colonel Blaskic wrote it himself, and it was done for him, it was signed for him by his deputy. I assume what happened was that Colonel Blaskic prepared the document, gave it to someone to type, and he may have been called to some task and gave it to his deputy in order to continue and sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I had not seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As late as August were you still outside of any investigation that went on surrounding Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D344, D344A for the English version, only the titles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you look at this report dated the 24th of April 1993, a list of the soldiers of the Viteska Brigade killed in conflict with the Muslim forces and the list of the wounded soldiers of the Viteska Brigade. On the 24th of April 1993. Did you know any of these people? Do you recognise this as an original document of the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with these data; however, I would like to make a comment about this document. Such a large number of killed and such a large number of wounded members of the Viteska Brigade alone testifies to the ferocity of the conflict and the strength of the attack of the BiH army when, within the Viteska Brigade, so many soldiers were killed and twice as many wounded in only four days of battle. I do not see any civilian casualties here, but I don't have it in my notes just now, but I will probably have the precise figures as to the number of Croats in Vitez killed during the conflict with units of the BH army from April 1993 until the Washington agreement. I would not like to give any rough figures, because imprecision is not appropriate, because every single human life is very valuable.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me proceed with the next document, and then we may have at least some approximations of the dead members of the HVO in Vitez alone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D345, D345A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is a list of the Defence Department of Vitez recording the members of the HVO killed. If we take note of the date when they were killed, we will see that it was in '93 until February of 1994, so that is the relevant period for this case. Will you please take a look at this list and look at the names, and according to this list, 541 men, or HVO members in Vitez were killed in the war with the BH army. So, tell the Court, is this a document from the Defence Department, and are there a number of persons on that list that you personally knew?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document of the Defence Department. I knew the head of the Defence Department, Stipo Krizanac, and these are relevant indicators and numbers regarding the Croats of Vitez killed in the war against the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, tell us, according to some, we call them norms or standards; what is usually the ratio between the killed and the wounded in a war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: According to my own knowledge, it should be three times more wounded than killed. But I will bring you also the figures regarding the wounded during my testimony here in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D346, D346A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a leaflet, and you will explain when and where you saw it. Let me read it. We have a big heading, it says "Combatants," and the Red Cross sign, and then the text. "This sign protects the wounded, sick and medical staff. For it to be effective you have to respect it. To respect it means not to target it, use it exclusively for protection of the wounded and sick, the persons taking care of them, hospitals and ambulances. Who can use this emblem, is the question. The answer: The Red Cross of your country, medical units, and the competent medical services, the International Committee of the Red Cross and its delegates. Misuse of the emblem, its use for camouflage, fraud, et cetera, represents a breach of international war law, respect the emblem at all times and in every place. Do not forget that one day you may also need its protection." Then in the second column it says: "Soldiers, in all circumstances, it is important to respect and protect." And then there is a picture of the Red Cross and the wounded, the wounded and the sick, medical units and personnel, prisoners of war, civilians. Then in bold print, "They are all entitled to humane treatment, without discrimination, humiliation or torture." Then we have a calendar for 1992 and 1993, below that the emblem of the Red Cross where it says: "The International Committee of the Red Cross is an independent humanitarian organisation and founder of the cross. As a neutral mediator, in the event of armed conflict or unrest, it endeavours on its own initiative or on the basis of the Geneva Convention to offer assistance and protection to victims of international and civil wars, unrest and tensions, thus contributing to world peace." We have the same such text underneath the calendar for 1993 and 1994. So, Brigadier, will you explain to the Court what this is? What are these copies of? Have you seen this before? If so, when?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, these are copies from a small brochure which we in the command of the Operative Zone, through our information and publicity department, received from our Red Cross and distributed to all our units that we were able to reach. When I say that we were able to reach, I'm not sure that we were able to send it to Zepce and Kiseljak or Vitez, but I know we distributed it in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There is a calendar for 1992, 1993 and 1994, what does that mean? Was this one or two brochures distributed in various periods of time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The calendar indicates that these brochures were distributed in 1992 and in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please. Who ordered that these brochures of the International Red Cross be distributed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I know that the commander of the Operative Zone, General Blaskic, gave instructions to his assistants for information and publicity to carry out the distribution of these brochures to subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: With what aim in mind?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In order that members of the HVO may be familiarised with this so as to be able to recognise and know what they should do under various circumstances they may encounter under conditions of war as it was being waged in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D347, D347A for the French version, 347B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the sake of clarification, we will go back in time for awhile. Colonel Blaskic did not start writing orders on the basis of the Geneva Conventions after Ahmici. He may have intensified them. We will go back in time and try to present to you what the Defence has managed to collect. We have a document of the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, but from 1992, the 5th of November in 1992. It is addressed to the municipal headquarters of the HVO in Novi Travnik, the defence headquarters in Novi Travnik, the regional headquarters of the BH army Zenica, and the HVO president in Novi Travnik. It reads: "Based on the agreement between the Commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, and Mr. Dzemo Merdan, Commander of the District Headquarters of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in order to prevent vandalism by individuals, I command: 1) That all measures be taken to prevent torching of houses of eminent citizens of Muslim nationality in your zone of responsibility. 2) Use all available forces and means to carry out this assignment and take the most rigorous measures against transgressors, in accordance with regulations on military discipline. Commander of the Headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a document addressed on the 5th of November, 1992 to the municipal headquarters of the HVO in Novi Travnik and the other addressees. Are you familiar with this document? Do you recognise Colonel Blaskic's signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recognise the signature. I'm familiar with the contents of the document, the reasons that prompted it. The tasks emanating from it are clear from the text. It was drafted after a minor conflict or, rather, an incident between HVO units within the territory of Novi Travnik municipality and BH army units in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just would like to ask the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: addressed to -- if you look at Article 1, I have got it in French, "Take all measures to prevent setting fire to houses of eminent citizens of Muslim nationality." Was there an equivalent for citizens of Croatian nationality, or was it simply a question of protecting the Muslims and why? The Croats didn't need to be protected, especially if it's an agreement between Merdan and Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not present at the meeting, nor do I know the contents of the talks between General Blaskic and Dzemo Merdan, but I assume that they agreed, that Colonel Blaskic issued such an order addressed to members of the HVO, and that Dzemo Merdan shall issue a similar order to the members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Thank you for this clarification, Judge Riad. I don't know whether it's a question of translation, but there is mention of the most eminent citizens of Muslim nationality. Maybe it's a question of translation. I turn myself to the Brigadier. "The most eminent citizens of Muslim nationality," what does that mean, as if there were Muslim citizens that were not eminent. I don't quite understand. Is it a question of translation? What is the Croatian version? What does it say exactly? The English version doesn't give me an explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no other explanation for this word, except for what it says here in the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could the interpreters help us? It says here, "The eminent citizens of Muslim nationality," the more eminent, the prominent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The more prominent, perhaps. Perhaps we can get more explanations later. Mr. Hayman, do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We'll look for one, but I've always assumed that the more eminent or more well-known citizens of any group might be more likely to be the target in a situation of conflict, the target of extremists, because they could be a symbol, if you will, of the group as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's leave it at that. Do you have any more questions about this document before we adjourn, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Mr. President. I've finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well then. After this afternoon, we're going to adjourn and resume tomorrow. Tomorrow is Thursday, Mr. Registrar, and we start at 10.00; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, exactly so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 6.16 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 1st day of October, 1998 at 10.00 a.m.
